votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

The Barstow Fire Protection District recently celebrated 100 years of service to our community! I was honored to present Fire Chief Justin Lendway with an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol in recognition of this important milestone. For a century, the department has https://t.co/5POg5n4q9I

I enjoyed meeting with Juan Rivera of Vibrant Villages Barstow to discuss their partnership with the Barstow Health Foundation and plans to develop a centralized resource hub connecting residents with healthcare providers, food assistance, and other essential services. These efforts highlight the importance of preventive healthcare, which is the focus of my bipartisan Preventive Health Savings Act. The legislation recently passed unanimously out of the House Budget Committee and would help Congress better account for the long-term fiscal benefits of preventive care. I appreciate Vibrant Villages' commitment to Barstow families and I'm honored to continue working together with them to improve access to these services.

Small businesses play a critical role in driving economic growth, creating jobs, and supporting families throughout our community. I recently joined the Greater High Desert Chamber of Commerce for their Valley Morning Insight event to discuss how federal fiscal policy and emerging technologies like artificial intelligence are shaping the future of our economy. We had a productive conversation about encouraging innovation, promoting responsible federal spending, and creating an environment where local businesses can grow and succeed. I appreciate the Chamber's continued efforts to support local businesses and strengthen our local economy.

Veterans Day is an important opportunity to reflect on the sacrifices made by generations of Americans in defense of our nation and the freedoms we enjoy. Their courage, selflessness, and commitment to protecting those freedoms deserve our continued recognition and gratitude. With the House in session this week, Heather and I took the opportunity to visit the World War II Memorial in Washington, D.C., to honor the brave men and women who have served our country.  To all of our Veterans and their families across our community, thank you for your service, sacrifice, and dedication to our nation!

Barstow has significant opportunities for economic growth, particularly with the development of BNSF's Barstow International Gateway project, which is expected to create new jobs, strengthen transportation infrastructure, and attract additional investment to our community. I recently met with Barstow Mayor Tim Silva to discuss the city's economic development priorities and how we can work together to support these opportunities. During our visit, I also had the pleasure of presenting Mayor Silva with an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol on July 4, 2026, in recognition of our nation's 250th anniversary. I look forward to continuing our partnership to support Barstow's growth and create new opportunities for local families.

Our first responders often face significant physical and emotional challenges while serving and protecting our community. That’s why I’ve cosponsored the bipartisan Helping Emergency Responders Overcome (HERO) Act to strengthen mental health support for firefighters, emergency medical personnel, and other public safety officers. This legislation would improve suicide prevention efforts, expand access to behavioral health and peer support programs, and help ensure those who dedicate their careers to protecting others have access to the resources they need.

Government impersonation schemes are becoming increasingly sophisticated, putting personal and financial information at risk. The Federal Trade Commission recently filed a lawsuit against two private companies accused of using misleading advertisements and websites to impersonate official government passport services and charge consumers unnecessary fees. When accessing federal services online, it is important to verify that you’re using official .gov websites, exercise caution with sponsored advertisements, and remain vigilant against suspicious requests for personal information or payment.

I was honored to be recognized by the Yucaipa City Council for my work advocating for the city's infrastructure priorities. From the Wilson III Basin flood control project to the proposed I-10/Wildwood Canyon Road Interchange, these investments are critical to improving public safety, strengthening infrastructure, and supporting Yucaipa's growth. I appreciate City Manager Dr. Sean Moore and the Yucaipa City Council for this recognition, and I'm looking forward to continuing our work together to address both the challenges and opportunities facing our community.

Today is Election Day! Voting is a critical part of our representative democracy, and I encourage all eligible voters in California's 23rd Congressional District who have not already cast their ballots to participate in this year's election. For information on polling locations and other voting resources, visit the California Secretary of State's website:https://t.co/ifL2yYxx8f

A recent California State Auditor report identified significant deficiencies in the state's management of Medi-Cal, including more than 26,000 high-risk providers whose billing practices had not been adequately reviewed. I've led a letter to the California Department of Health Care Services demanding answers about these findings and the steps being taken to investigate potentially improper payments, recover taxpayer dollars, and prevent future fraud. Medi-Cal provides critical care to millions of Californians, and every dollar lost to fraud is a dollar that is not available to help our most vulnerable citizens access the care they need.

I am pleased to see that $233.6 million in new federal funding is coming to California through the Rural Health Transformation Program. Rural healthcare providers face significant challenges in recruiting and retaining medical professionals, maintaining access to specialty care, and coordinating services across healthcare systems. This funding will help address those challenges by strengthening our healthcare workforce, expanding telehealth services, and improving coordination between providers. These investments are critical to improving access to quality healthcare for families in California's 23rd District and across our state. Learn more here: https://t.co/WXSgUdAvqC

I was delighted to join local water leaders for the dedication of the Santa Ana Watershed Hydro Authority. This partnership between four local water agencies will oversee seven hydroelectric facilities, helping support reliable, renewable energy generation while protecting our community’s water supply. Thank you to everyone involved in this effort to make better use of our existing infrastructure and strengthen local water and energy resources!

Drivers in Washington state currently pay an average of $5.34 per gallon for gas, while Californians are paying $6.08, nearly 75 cents more per gallon. roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Combating Organized Retail Crime Act (H R 2853)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill expands federal enforcement of criminal offenses related to organized retail and supply chain crime. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
